title: ‘World War Z’ Director Marc Forster Adapting Jamie Scallion’s Revenge Thriller ‘Nines’ For TV With Renée Wolfe, Me+You Productions & Fremantle
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart , Stewart Clarke October 8, 2026 1:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Marc Forster (left) and Jamie Scallion Gallup/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures EXCLUSIVE: World War Z and Quantum of Solace director Marc Forster is turning his hand to TV by directing an adaptation of Jamie Scallion ’s buzzy upcoming thriller Nines . Nines, which follows a man in jail intent on revenge, was snapped up by Forster and Renée Wolfe’s indie 2DUX² along with I Am… producer Me+You Productions following what they termed a “fiercely competitive auction.” The show is being forged as a high-end returning TV series and publisher Transworld has already acquired world English-language rights to the novel plus its sequel, which won’t publish until 2028 and 2029 respectively. Fremantle , which has a first-look deal with Me+You, is selling the show globally. Related Stories News Sharon Levy Moves To Fremantle After Endemol Shine Exit Executives Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years The titular character in Nines is an orphan, pianist, father, widower and killer. Serving a life sentence in Britain’s most secure jail for killing one of the men who murdered his wife, he now wants the rest of them, and to track down the son they took from him. In prison, his mentor, master forger and zen master Suranga moulds him into the machine that will finish the job, but he must then break out into a world that has changed. Watch on Deadline BAFTA-nominee Forster will direct the first block of episodes and remain “closely involved throughout the series, helping shape its visual language and creative tone,” the team said. He and the creative team are now casting and speaking to writers. Forster is better known for his work on the big screen. His credits include disaster movie World War Z with Brad Pitt, James Bond’s Quantum of Solace, Finding Neverland and A Man Called Otto. On the small screen, he directed two episodes and exec produced Prime Video’s Hand of God , which starred Ron Perlman as a corrupt judge who suffers a breakdown. Forster is working with producing partner Wolfe and their 2DUX² outfit along with Me+You, which is run by Krish Majumdar and Richard Yee. Me+You is probably best known for Dominic Savage’s I Am… female-led drama anthology for Channel 4, which won Kate Winslet a BAFTA and has its next instalment coming up with Nicola Coughlan and Joe Cole. Scallion, meanwhile, has had an intriguing path to Nines. He was lead singer in rock band Officer Kicks and went on to collaborate with Irish band The Script on a YA book series called The Rock ‘n’ Roll Diaries. In 2025 he co-wrote another YA novel, The Last Song on Earth, with broadcaster Dave Berry. Forster and Wolfe said Nines Season 1 should “feel like an event – and the beginning of something much larger.” “We want Nines to strike a very particular balance of intriguing, emotional characters juxtaposed with fresh and relevant action sequences that further the depth of the story,” they added. “What excites us is that Nines feels built for the screen, with a character and a world that can keep expanding.” Majumdar and Yee called Nines a “propulsive, funny and unexpectedly moving thriller.” “Having a world-class filmmaker like Marc directing is a real coup,” they said. “We can’t wait to work with Jamie on this adaptation of his stunning debut.. We believe Nines has every chance of becoming an iconic anti-hero for the screen.” The deal for Nines was negotiated for Scallion by Eugenie Furniss at 42 and spearheaded for Me+You by Raffaella De Angelis, Head of Literary Acquisitions, Global Drama at Fremantle. Wolfe and Forster are repped by Ari Greenburg and Austin Vaziri at WME. full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Lightdox Acquires Sales Rights To ‘Nostalgia For The Future,’ Documentary On Enigmatic Filmmaker Chris Marker Narrated By Charlotte Rampling ‘Ash And Crayons’ Trailer: In Evgeny Afineevsky’s Film, Wounded Ukrainian Children Show Will To Survive And Thrive Doc Talk Podcast: Producer James Costa On Deadline’s For The Love Of Docs Series, Oscar Season And ‘NAZA’ Controversy View All October 8, 2026 1:34am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Nostalgia for the Future' Visualantics/SeriousFilm/Cobra Films/Ghirigori EXCLUSIVE: Lightdox has acquired international sales rights to Nostalgia for the Future leading into Film Fest Gent in Belgium where the documentary screens on Sunday. The film narrated by Oscar-nominated actress Charlotte Rampling examines the enigmatic filmmaker Chris Marker (1921-2012), one of the most influential figures in the history of cinema. The Belgium–Netherlands–Italy co-production, directed by Brecht Debackere , made its world premiere in May at the Cannes Film Festival. “Chris Marker, filmmaker, photographer, writer and multimedia artist behind such landmark works as La Jetée and Sans Soleil , spent much of his life deliberately avoiding the public eye,” notes a synopsis. “Famously elusive, he rarely gave interviews and would sometimes send photographs of his cats instead of portraits of himself. He once described himself as the ‘best-known author of unknown films.’ Related Stories Acquisitions Lightdox Acquires 'Auber 89' Ahead Of Doc's World Premiere at Venice Film Festival Sidebar Giornate Degli Autori News Anthony Hopkins & Charlotte Rampling To Star In 'The Species' ‘Nostalgia for the Future’ Visualantics/SeriousFilm/Cobra Films/Ghirigori “In Nostalgia for the Future , Debackere enters the labyrinth of Marker’s legacy through the 550 boxes of his personal archive, now held by the Cinémathèque française. Guided by Rampling’s distinctive voice, an unnamed archivist moves through photographs, documents, film fragments and personal traces, attempting to reconstruct the man who chose to disappear behind his own images.” Watch on Deadline Instead of a traditional biography, the film approaches Marker “through the associative logic of his work,” according to a release. “The archive becomes a living system of memory, while Marker’s images become ‘time machines,’ fragments through which the past, present and possible futures begin to overlap.” ‘Nostalgia for the Future’ Visualantics/SeriousFilm/Cobra Films/Ghirigori Nostalgia for the Future , a co-production between Visualantics, SeriousFilm, Cobra Films and Ghirigori, is produced by Steven Dhoedt. In a statement, Lightdox CEO Anna Berthollet commented, “Chris Marker left behind an archive as enigmatic as the man himself. Brecht Debackere has found a remarkably cinematic way into this world, creating not simply a portrait of Marker, but a meditation on images, memory and the way we imagine the future. A film that speaks directly to what Lightdox looks for: bold, author-driven documentaries with a distinctive cinematic language and the power to open new ways of seeing.” Brecht Debackere ( Exprmntl ) wrote and directed the film. The directors of photography are Jerome De Gerlache, Alexi Van Hennecker, and Ben Grinand; Beppe Leonetti edited the film. The original score is by Rutger Zuydervelt and Niels Borrey. In addition to Sunday’s debut at Film Fest Gent, Nostalgia for the Future screens at the festival on Monday and Thursday. full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Alternativa Distribution Takes ‘No Good Men’ & ‘Four Daughters’ To MIPCOM ‘World War Z’ Director Marc Forster Adapting Jamie Scallion’s Revenge Thriller ‘Nines’ For TV With Renée Wolfe, Me+You Productions & Fremantle The Deadline Dozen: The Hottest Scripted Shows Heading To MIPCOM Including ‘Baywatch’, ‘Einstein’ & ‘Maya’ Starring Bella Ramsey View All July 15, 2026 2:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Zoljargal Purevdash's 'If Only I Could Hibernate' Alternativa Distribition EXCLUSIVE: Alternativa has launched a distribution arm that will sell impact-driven films to broadcasters and streamers. Alternativa Distribution will be run by former yesDocu and TikTok exec Avital Lavi. It goes out of the gate with a ten-movie slate including Zoljargal Purevdash’s If Only I Could Hibernate , which played in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes . A Poet , from Simón Mesa Soto, also played in Un Certain Regard, and was awarded the Jury Prize. We previously had the news that a U.S. remake is in the works. Other titles on the slate include Sunshine from Filipino director Antoinette Jadaone and Maksud Hossain’s Saba . Related Stories News 'Elle' & 'The Man I Love' Producer Saïd Ben Saïd Teams With 'Between The Temples' Director Nathan Silver For U.S. Remake Of Cannes Winner 'A Poet' -- Cannes Market News Colombian Filmmaker & Cannes Winner Simón Mesa Soto Signs With UTA Alternativa is a not-for-profit org that supports impact films from the Global South. Having started out as an awards program for films from Central Asia, Alternativa then initiated a full-fledged festival. There have been editions was in Indonesia and Colombia and next year’s event will be in Africa. Watch on Deadline The newly minted Alternativa Distribution division will work on what Lavi describes as a “fair play model.” Speaking to Deadline, the Berlin-based exec explained more: “We negotiate with the rights holders for acquisitions and offer them a fair minimum guarantee. We pay that immediately, and then once we start distributing, we do revenue shares.” She added that Alternativa will foot the bill for dubbing and subtitling to help make the films ready for local channels and platforms. “So many of the films from the Global South cannot reach audiences because nobody wants to do the heavy lifting of localization. It’s resources, time, it’s money… so we will cover that.” The goal is to sell movies outside of a theatrical release and shop first-window rights to broadcasters and streamers. Because of the model and wider aim of promoting films from the Global South, the good news for buyers is the license fees will be modest. “We believe it’s a self-sustaining model, both in the aspect of sustaining the local film industries and also sustaining the distribution operation, and because this is a not-for-profit operation, we don’t expect to have [high] license fees,” Lavi said. Five of the ten films on the launch slate screened at the Alternativa Film Festival. Lavi said that it has scouts in local markets and will be looking for titles to add to its lineup. “Our selection is based not only on artistic excellence and impact, but also on the films’ accessibility potential. We will take films that resonate on the emotional side and make people feel empathy, hope and sorrow and all these things that could ultimately manage to create some sort of cognitive change.” Alternativa is backed by the ride-hailing and transportation business inDrive. The goal for Alternativa Distribution is to bring films from the Global South to an audience beyond the local markets and festival circuit, Lavi said. “The distribution arm is scaling them up to more audiences. We wanted to take them way beyond the festival circuit.” Alternativa Distribution will be at MIPCOM and the major film and TV markets. title: Marco Bellocchio’s ‘Falcon’ Sets Sales & Announces Louis Garrel In Role Of Fiat Boss John Elkann
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie ‘NAZA’ Producer James Wilson Addresses “Hysterical, Vituperative” Israeli Government Backlash Against Directors Oscars: Rwanda Makes History As ‘Ben’Imana’ Becomes First Official Entry; Alexander Set U.S. & UK Release Hande Erçel To Star In Nader Saeivar’s Berlin-Set Drama ‘Diaspora’ View All October 8, 2026 2:02am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Louis Garrel, Marco Bellocchio, Pierfrancesco Favino Riccardo Ghilardi, Anna Camerlingo, Pablo Arroyo Rai Cinema International Distribution has boarded sales on Marco Bellocchio ’s financial thriller Falcon , inspired by the life of late Fiat-Chrysler automobile exec Sergio Marchionne, as it films in Toronto. In new casting additions, previously announced lead Pierfrancesco Favino is being joined by Louis Garrel , Benedetta Cimatti and Barbara Ronchi, with the participation of Valeria Bruni Tedeschi. The picture delves into the story of the Marchionne, the Italian-Canada automobile exec credited with reviving Italy ’s Turin-based car company Fiat in the 2000s and merging it with then ailing U.S. auto manufacturer Chrysler. Related Stories News 'Maserati: The Brothers' Actress Maya Talem Signs With MAD Celebrity News Oscars: Italy Submits Paolo Strippoli's 'The Spiral' For Best International Feature Film It will recount how Sergio Marchionne (Favino) came to the rescue of Italy’s most famous car manufacturer in 2004 as it lay on the verge of collapse in the wake of the death of its longtime boss, the legendary industrialist Gianni Agnelli. Watch on Deadline Ruthless and visionary, Marchionne axed the top management. He then took Agnelli’s grandson, John Elkann (Garrel), under his wing to teach the young heir, suddenly burdened with the family’s legacy, the art of command. Marchionne then took on the U.S. car manufacturer General Motors, disentangling Fiat from a disadvantage strategic alliance, and went on to save rival Chrysler from bankruptcy by merging it with Fiat. Falcon is co-written by Marco Bellocchio with Ludovica Rampoldi, Andrea Di Stefano, Stefano Rulli and with the participation of Oliviero Del Papa. Talking to Deadline about the project last year , Bellocchio said of Marchionne: “I’m fascinated by his journey and his ability, as an Italian who stood up to American big business, to defend Fiat and then even take over Chrysler, which was bankrupt, to make a major group.” He also revealed that the title of Falcon is inspired by the fact that Marchionne would always travel on a Falcon business jet. “He would travel went back and forth from Turin on a Falcon, so we’ve given it this title,” he said. Falcon is produced by Kavac Film, Rai Cinema, with Emotion Network in collaboration with STLA Europe. The feature has already shot for two weeks in September in Toronto and Niagara Falls, moving to the Piedmont region of Italy and to Rome, and then returning to Canada and the United States in early 2027. 01 Distribution will release the film in Italy. The project reunites Bellocchio with a number of longtime creative collaborators, including production designer Andrea Castorina, costume designer Daria Calvelli, and editor Francesca Calvelli, all of whom worked on Bellocchio on projects including The Traitor , Exterior Night and Kidnapped . He is also joined for the first time by director of photography Matteo Cocco ( The Weight , Hidden Away ). Harmonia is a rare UK-Greek co-pro coming from Adolescence co-producer Warp Films , Athens’ Neda Films, ITV Studios and Greek pubcaster ERT. In Harmonia, Algar is the AI’s creator, Shona Casey, while Ardant plays the resort’s former owner. In the resort and wellness facility, technology meets escapism and every guest’s desire can be fulfilled. It reflects things we all aspire to, but also fear. It’s a modern-day Frankenstein story of a scientist who would be God, and their extraordinary creation, where it becomes increasingly unclear whether the AI is the monster, or whether the humans are. Related Stories News Nick Curwin, Founder Of British Production Houses Dragonfly & The Garden, Retiring From Indie Incubator Matisse News 'Smilla's Sense Of Snow' Series Settles At AMC+ Chloe Lea ( Dune: Prophecy, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms ) plays a young member of staff that the AI becomes obsessed with, while the cast includes Oliver Chris ( Rivals, The Crown ), Abubakar Salim ( House of the Dragon, Raised by Wolves ), Goran Bogdan ( Legacy of Spies, The Last Panthers ), Theo Augier ( XO Kitty, Jay Kelly ) and George Ioannides ( Guys and Dolls, Industry ). Completing the ensemble are Greek stars Pygmalion Dadakaridis ( The Other Me, Rififi ), rising TV and theatre actor Konstantinos Zografos (The Judge, Derti) Antigoni Frida ( Grand Hotel, Sauté ) and newcomer Zoe-Stella Nikolaou. Watch on Deadline The coming together of UK and Greek teams sees the series created by Peter Carlton, Lefteris Charitos, Amanda Livanou and Hanna Jameson. Charitos, director of Wild Bees , one of Greek television’s biggest ever successes, directs all six episodes. Jameson, best-selling author of The Last and writer on the upcoming Netflix series The Twin starring Jamie Dornan, is lead writer, with episodes from Alki Papastathopoulos and Panayotis Christopoulos. Jameson said: “With this project, I had the chance to tell a truly meaningful story full of funny, strange, and complicated characters, reminiscent of the legendary genre shows I grew up watching. It’s been so exciting to explore how our relationship with technology has changed so fast in such a short period of time, evolving faster than our ability to understand the personal and global consequences. When I’m gripped by a great show everything else falls away, the house could burn down around me and I wouldn’t notice, and I hope that people feel the same way about Harmonia .” Shooting takes place on location in Athens at Cape Sounio resort and Kapa2 Studios ahead of launch in 2027. Harmonia is produced in association with and distributed internationally by ITV Studios. It is co-financed by ITV Studios, and Greek public broadcaster ERT, with development support from the Hellenic Film & Audiovisual Fund and Creative Europe Media. title: BBC Apologizes “Unreservedly” And Removes Article Accusing PinkNews Founder Of Sexual Misconduct
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Joe Sugg & Caspar Lee’s MVE Expands With CAA & WME Hires In U.S. Apple TV Buys Tropic Noir Series ‘Dustfall’ Starring Anna Torv PBS Masterpiece’s ‘Maigret’ Finds UK Home View All October 8, 2026 3:53am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Leon Neal/Getty The BBC has “apologized unreservedly for the defamatory allegations” made in a documentary and accompanying article about the founder of one of the UK’s leading LGBTQ+ publications and his husband. The BBC this morning removed from its website the original PinkNews article. The documentary came off iPlayer last year after its window ran down. The corporation has agreed to pay compensation to PinkNews founder Benjamin Cohen and his husband Anthony James. In a joint statement on PinkNews, Cohen and James said the BBC had “reinforced one of the most damaging homophobic tropes” by “falsely portraying us as engaging in sexual misconduct and pressuring female employees over surrogacy.” Related Stories News BBC Boss Matt Brittin Sets Out Silicon Valley-Style Revolution At British Broadcaster News 'Doctor Who' Bids Revealed: Jed Mercurio Leads Pitch To Regenerate BBC Series, As STV Studios Plans To Transport TARDIS To Scotland The BBC launched the documentary, PinkNews: Behind Closed Doors, and an accompanying article titled “PinkNews bosses accused of sexual misconduct” in late 2024. The doc and article said the BBC had spoken with 30 current and former employees, some of whom told the BBC they had experienced bullying and sexual misconduct from Cohen and James. The BBC also reported that several people had said some young female members of staff had been asked to act as the couple’s surrogates. Watch on Deadline Cohen and James’ High Court statement read out after the settlement called the allegations “serious, false, defamatory… and extremely harmful to the claimants’ reputations.” It noted that, as a result of the doc and article, Cohen and James were subject to additional investigations by CAFCASS (Children and Family Court Advisory and Support Service) ahead of a parental order hearing at the Family Court in respect of their son, who had been born via surrogate. The BBC’s counsel responded by saying the corporation “accepts everything” and “retracts and apologises unreservedly for the defamatory allegatios made in the programme and the article.” A BBC spokeswoman told Deadline: “The BBC has reached a settlement with Ben Cohen and Anthony James. We will not be issuing any further comment.” Cohen and James’ PinkNews statement said: “By falsely portraying us as engaging in sexual misconduct and pressuring female employees over surrogacy, the BBC reinforced one of the most damaging homophobic tropes: that gay men are sexual predators who pose a threat to others. These were allegations that should never have been broadcast.” They added that while they can now “finally begin to move forward,” the BBC “needs to carefully consider and learn from the impact that its reckless journalism has had on a young family’s lives.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: 1 Comments

title: Hande Erçel To Star In Nader Saeivar’s Berlin-Set Drama ‘Diaspora’
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Oscars: Rwanda Makes History As ‘Ben’Imana’ Becomes First Official Entry; Alexander Set U.S. & UK Release Hande Erçel To Star In Nader Saeivar’s Berlin-Set Drama ‘Diaspora’ Marco Bellocchio’s ‘Falcon’ Sets Sales & Announces Louis Garrel In Role Of Fiat Boss John Elkann View All October 8, 2026 4:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hande Erçel Atwood Films, Sky Films EXCLUSIVE: Turkish star Hande Erçel has been unveiled as the lead actress in Iranian director and screenwriter Nadar Saeivar ’s upcoming Germany -set drama Diaspora ahead of an early 2027 shoot. Berlin-based director Saeivar, whose recent directorial credits include No End (2022), The Witness (2024) and Hijamat (2026), is also known internationally for his work with Jafar Panahi. He shared an original screenplay Oscar nomination this year with Panahi for Cannes Palme d’Or winner It Was Just An Accident , and has also collaborated with the director on a number of other works. Related Stories News 'Where's Wanda' Season 2: Watch Trailer For Apple TV's Darkly Comic German Series From UFA Fiction News Studiocanal Announces Wrap Of Final Film In Ambitious German-Language 'Woodwalkers' Trilogy Saeivar’s upcoming feature in the director’s seat will star Erçel as Merve, an educated, middle-class Turkish woman trying to rebuild her life and that of her 12-year-old son in Germany after the tragic death of her husband in Turkey . Watch on Deadline As she attempts to move on from a painful past, she finds works in the language school of a German family expecting their second child. After a meet-up between Merve, her son and the German family, she falls victim to inappropriate physical contact by the family’s 15-year-old son named Luca. Torn between remaining silent and speaking out, she decides to inform the boy’s father after the harassment recurs. However, the family refuses to believe Merve and turns the accusations against her, making her the target of severe slander. As a widowed immigrant living alone with her 12-year-old son in a foreign country, she is forced into a gruelling battle against both the justice system and societal prejudices. The family’s refusal to accept their child’s wrongdoing deepens Merve’s isolation. Striving to stay strong for her son, the young woman finds herself dragged into an exhausting struggle between law and conscience to prove her innocence. Erçel, who is known for her roles in Turkish box office hit Intoxicated by Love and Netflix show Chasing the Wind , will travel to Berlin about a month prior to shooting to begin character development, language training and creative rehearsals. She will be joined in the cast by Moritz Bleibtreu as the father of the German family with further international cast members due to be unveiled in the coming weeks. Produced jointly by Said Nur Akkus at Berlin-based Arthood Films and Emre Oskay at Istanbul-based Sky Films, Diaspora will take place entirely in Berlin, and the production will be in German, English, and Turkish. Saeivar, who was born and grew up in northwestern Iran with Turkish roots, previously explored the migrant experience in his adopted home of Berlin in Hijamat about a man hailing from the city’s Turkish community who discovers his brother is gay. “ Diaspora is born from an urgent need to re-examine the intricate, often silent dynamics between the East and the West, a relationship too frequently shaped by systemic misunderstandings, subtle prejudices, and historical projections,” said Saeivar in a director’s note. “For decades, the Western gaze has tended to view the East through a lens of either exoticism or perpetual trauma, reducing individual human complexities to mere cultural stereotypes or political statistics. When individuals from the East arrive in the West seeking peace, they often find themselves navigating an unwritten social hierarchy where their voices are muted, their boundaries violated under the guise of “cultural differences,” and their dignity traded for survival.” “This film is not merely a story of displacement; it is a call for a profound shift in perspective. True coexistence cannot be built on passive tolerance or structural superiority. A peaceful shared future demands authentic empathy.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: Comments

title: Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc ‘Dependence’ Back Home To London — LFF
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc ‘Dependence’ Back Home To London — LFF Brad Bird On The 30-Year Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To The Big Screen — London Film Festival London Film Festival Opens With Passionate ‘Elsinore’ Homecoming Screening View All October 8, 2026 4:36am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The 2026 London Film Festival rolls into action this week. And among the headline international galas, there is once again a strong collection of homegrown titles. The most exciting is perhaps Dependence , a moving, formally experimental documentary directed by debut filmmaker Grace Harper Brighouse . Dependence premiered earlier this year at Camden, where it won the festival’s Harrell Award. The film examines the filmmaker’s strained relationship with her father, an estrangement caused by his OxyContin addiction, using a collection of home movies she shot from childhood through to adulthood, including film school rushes. Related Stories News Brad Bird On The 30-Year Journey To Bring 'Ray Gunn' To The Big Screen -- London Film Festival News London Film Festival Opens With Passionate 'Elsinore' Homecoming Screening “It was in 2013. I was making my first film at film school, about a strip pub in High Wycombe. I was having the best time,” Brighouse explains of the film’s origins. “But I was very aware that I didn’t know what I was doing. I didn’t have enough time to make the film the way I wanted.” Brighouse says her brother suggested returning home to make a film about their dad and his dying dog, Charlie. “Every year, if my dad and I hadn’t been speaking, he would say, ‘Charlie’s going to die. He’s never going to make it through the winter.’ It gave us both an off-ramp: we could be together without having to apologise to each other for whatever the reason was that we weren’t speaking,” she says. “So I came back. I’d been watching a lot of Russian documentaries, and I was really enjoying the smoke, the framing, and the very pretentious, arthouse documentary shots that I still love so much. But I realised that it had been quite a long time. I guess this is what a camera does: it lets you observe things that you don’t usually observe, particularly in your closest relationships.” Brighouse’s brother died suddenly, and the footage sat dormant for many years. “I couldn’t really watch it for a very long time. A dear friend of mine, Eleanor Mortimer, logged it for me so I could look at it without having to watch it. It was such a gift because I couldn’t do it myself.” Brighouse says she later felt an unexplainable urge to return to the material. “I would look at it and think, ‘Okay, what was here? Let me look at this.’ Slowly, I understood that I wasn’t done with that film, but it wasn’t the film I was making anymore,” she says. “So, what had it become?” The Camden programmers described Dependence as “a funny, tender, and poignant essay on family bonds.” Indeed, Dependence is a thoughtful exploration of addiction and the unique power of paternal love. The film has a breezy construction. There are time jumps, and images are presented in multiple formats. Brighouse also avoids talking heads or any of the visual tropes we’ve come to associate with films about families and addiction. She cites RaMell Ross’s wonderfully transgressive Hale County This Morning, This Evening as an influence. “That film unlocked a way for me to think about storytelling and time, and about creating a visual language that is different from the guidebook,” Brighouse says. Brighouse is credited as the director and cinematographer on Dependence . There is additional cinematography by Roger Chapman, Ronnie McQuillan, and Tom Besley. Vera Simmonds was the editor, and the film was produced by Caitlin Mae Burke and Alistair Payne-James (140 Films). Brighouse describes a scrappy production. “We had to get to a rough cut by scraping together very little money through artist residencies and paid time. Everyone had other jobs while doing it,” she says, adding that she hopes the film can find and engage with a large audience. “I hope we’ve made something where, in the end, you think, ‘I really just want to talk to my family member and tell them I love them,’” Brighouse says. “That sounds trite, but I hope the film can sit in that space of complex, messy familial love, as well as all the issues it touches on.” 140 Films is heading sales on the project. The film screens Sunday, October 11th, at the LFF . title: PBS Masterpiece’s ‘Maigret’ Finds UK Home

BBC Studios-owned UKTV has taken both seasons of the Georges Simenon adaptation for its U&Drama network plus U streaming service, coming as part of a 114-hour content deal with Banijay Rights. Produced by Wolf Hall maker Playground in association with Banijay Rights, the series stars Benjamin Wainwright as Chief Inspector Jules Maigret, Stefanie Martini as Madame Louise Maigret and Blake Harrison as Joseph Torrence. It reinvents one of the world’s most recognizable crime brands, following the chief inspector and his team of loyal, maverick detectives solving crimes in Paris. It has been adapted plenty down the years including for a 2016 ITV series starring Rowan Atkinson. title: BBC Chief Meets Netflix CEO & Other Streamers In Bid To Forge “Strategic Partnerships”
full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Staff Raise Concerns About Director-General’s Praise For AI-Generated ‘Doctor Who’ BBC Chief Meets Netflix CEO & Other Streamers In Bid To Forge “Strategic Partnerships” ‘Baby Reindeer’ Battle Reignites: Netflix Suffers Blow In Bid To Get Fiona Harvey Lawsuit Spiked View All October 8, 2026 5:07am Add us as a Google Preferred Source BBC boss Matt Brittin Getty EXCLUSIVE : BBC director general Matt Brittin has spent time in recent weeks meeting with the leaders of U.S. streamers in an effort to showcase more of the corporation’s content. Brittin, a former Google executive, told staff on Wednesday that he had met with the “global leadership” of Netflix , Amazon Prime Video , Apple TV, and YouTube in an effort to forge “strategic partnerships.” Deadline understands, for example, that Brittin sat down with Greg Peters when the Netflix co-CEO visited London in recent weeks. Related Stories News BBC Apologizes "Unreservedly" And Removes Article Accusing PinkNews Founder Of Sexual Misconduct News Brad Bird On The 30-Year Journey To Bring 'Ray Gunn' To The Big Screen -- London Film Festival Brittin has put partnerships at the heart of his agenda in his early months at the BBC, though it is not yet clear how closer collaboration could work with U.S. streamers. Watch on Deadline The director general told staff: “Since I’ve been here, we’ve met with the global leadership of Netflix, Amazon, Apple and YouTube to talk about not just the individual things that we’re doing, but what if we step back and say, ‘What are all the things we could do to help the BBC to transform at this time?’ “Because of our reputation and our trust internationally, I think we can get a lot more out of players like that, as well as the many partners we have in other parts of the BBC as well.” Brittin added that he wants to ensure that the BBC’s content is more “prominent” on Netflix and YouTube, and has previously spoken about making more BBC News output available on these services. In a deal that predated his arrival, the BBC agreed to produce original YouTube shows for the first time under a pact with the Google-owned video service. Brittin’s proposals are also in step with the British government’s plan to compel YouTube to promote public service content. YouTube has expressed reservations about this, calling it “forced prominence.” Brittin’s comments on streamer partnerships come as Reuters reported that the BBC and Channel 4 are scoping out a joint-venture deal. This could include BBC Studios combining UKTV with Channel 4’s advertising operations, channels including E4 and Film4, and its streaming service. Channel 4’s main network would not be included in such an arrangement, Reuters reported. Brittin and Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra have spoken openly about a partnership, including iPlayer hosting Channel 4 shows. Dogra has, however, warned against the BBC acquiring full control of Channel 4. A BBC spokesperson said: “We won’t be providing any comment, but as we’ve said before, we believe increased collaboration between all public service broadcasters is vital to ensure the industry thrives in a highly competitive global marketplace.” Channel 4 said: “We won’t be commenting on any speculation but we welcome and support greater collaboration between public service media and strongly believe working together can strengthen impact, innovation and sustainability in UK broadcasting. Channel 4 and the BBC already have a successful commercial relationship, involving ad sales for UKTV and the carriage of U on 4Streaming.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: 1 Comments

title: Eyeing More ‘Minecrafts’ And ‘Fallouts’, Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Joe Rogan Sets Multi-Year Extension With Spotify Eyeing More ‘Minecrafts’ And ‘Fallouts’, Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games ‘Beyond The Spider-Verse’ Director Bob Persichetti On “Limitless” Fan Expectations And “Never Saying No” View All October 8, 2026 5:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jack Black promotes 'A Minecraft Movie' Courtesy Microsoft Xbox , hoping to replicate the success of franchises like Minecraft and Fallout , is launching a new division called XP designed to extend properties beyond video games . The XP name is described as a play on “experience points.” It has four main components: Xbox Pictures for film and TV adaptations; Xbox Products for licensing and merchandise; Xbox Partnerships for sponsors and brand partners; and Xbox Places for broadcast and in-person events. “Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them,” CEO Asha Sharma explained to employees in a staff memo Thursday. Related Stories Casting Walton Goggins Joins Michael B. Jordan And Austin Butler In 'Miami Vice '85' At Universal News Xbox Continues "Reset" With Additional Layoffs And Restructuring Expanding properties beyond video games then creates a virtuous cycle, Xbox says. Fallout titles on Xbox Game Pass saw a 5x increase in hours played during Fallout ‘s first season on Prime Video. Minecraft saw over a 75% increase in weekly active users of the game year-over-year since the movie’s release in the spring of 2025. Watch on Deadline Hollywood, meanwhile, has finally found its groove with adapting games into films and series. Sony revived Resident Evil last month and HBO drew big viewership and critical praise with The Last of Us , just to name a couple of recent success stories. The XP news comes after Xbox has initiated a self-described “reset” with multiple rounds of layoffs and restructured its studio businesses to adapt to a changing operating environment in the games sector. In 2023, Microsoft acquired Activision Blizzard for $69 billion at a moment when mobile and casual gaming was starting to upend the traditional console business. Kayleen Walters, a former Lucasfilm executive, has been named president of XP. She is expected to build a team at the division from staffer both internal and external. Maria Angelidou-Smith is joining Xbox as CEO of Mojang and Minecraft after nearly a decade at Meta. After spending 13 years at Lucasfilm working on Star Wars, Walters helped grow Xbox’s consumer products arm into a mult-billion-dollar business with more than 250 licenses. She was an executive producer of A Minecraft Movie , and is a full producer on its sequel, which is currently in production. “Fans don’t just play our franchises,” Walters wrote to employees in an email to her team. “They watch them, wear them, attend them, celebrate them, and connect with them in countless ways.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: Comments
